title: The Singer conjecture in dimension four
main_claim: For every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex Q of formal dimension 4 (any orientation character), and so for every closed aspherical topological 4-manifold, b_p^(2) of the universal cover vanishes for p≠2. The essential step is b_1^(2)=0. It is proved by contradiction: a positive b_1^(2) would yield a finite-energy boundary continuum L that has no cut point, is locally connected, has dim ≤1 and Čech H^1(L;F2)=0. Such a space would be a nondegenerate dendrite with no cut point, which is impossible.

issues.location: pretree.tex, Lemma pret:parabolic-cuts (and Prop. pret:package references)
issues.description: Ruling out a nontrivial dendritic quotient, and showing that all cut points are parabolic, depends entirely on two cited results: Bowditch, Connectedness properties of limit sets, Lemma 1.4 (no convergence action on a dendrite without a two-ended splitting), and Bowditch, Treelike structures, Theorem 6.1. The paper restates their hypotheses (finitely presented, one-ended, no infinite torsion subgroup, minimal convergence action on a continuum that need not be locally connected). I could not check these statements against the sources. Nothing in the paper's use of them is wrong, but this is the one place where the argument rests on external statements I did not verify.
issues.evidence: "Bowditch's dendrite obstruction [Lemma 1.4]{Bowditch1999Connected} applies to a finitely presented one-ended group ... provided every two-ended subgroup over which the group splits is parabolic on that dendrite."

issues.description: An observation about scope, not an error. Apart from finite presentation and torsion-freeness, the argument uses only H^1(Γ;F2Γ)=H^2(Γ;F2Γ)=0 and the absence of splittings over finite or two-ended subgroups (from H^1(Γ;k[Γ/J])≅H_3(J;k)). So it implicitly proves b_1^(2)=0 for a much larger class of groups than PD4 groups. I found no counterexample: for hyperbolic groups the claim agrees with the conformal-dimension / ℓ^p-cohomology picture, where one-dimensional boundaries have nonzero Čech H^1. Still, the stronger implicit statement deserves independent scrutiny.
issues.evidence: Sections 3-9 use only Lemma found:duality, found:ends, found:trees and found:gradient as group-theoretic input.

coverage: I read every section of the LaTeX source in build/ (introduction, foundations, compactification, dynamics, boundary-topology, pretree, blocks, annuli, path-pushing, conclusion, consequences) and checked each proof step by step. Steps checked: the PD4 reductions (Wall finiteness, torsion-freeness, L2 duality with the orientation cover, H^i(Γ;kΓ)=0 for i=1,2 through homological Shapiro, one-endedness, and the crossing-count bound for tree actions); the minimal-energy potential and its connected level sides; the good-box finiteness argument; the localized coordinates and the near-path lemma; the ℓ^2 edge lengths and the connectedness of B; the convergence-action proof, the parabolic comparison and minimality; thin walls giving H^1-measure zero and the multiplicity-2 covers giving dim≤1; the Čech H^1 argument through a finite-support correction and H^2(Γ;kΓ)=0; the ordinal argument giving an invariant finite-interval class; the block graph, the retraction and the absence of cut points in L; the extension lemma and component labels; the annulus system and depth finiteness; depth comparison (pruning and concatenation of chains); translated deletions, eventual labels, the majority threshold and refinement; and the Hausdorff-limit local connectivity and the dendrite contradiction. I did not check the cited Bowditch results against their sources.
